lines.text: Then leave the equipment alone. We'll look from the entrance and decide whether we should go any farther.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Don't like the room dimensions? Write to the owner. If you can dig up an address.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She answers too quickly. Wendy glances at a narrow stair along the wall, then back at the children. Pacifica notices, but doesn't get a chance to ask.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Something darkens beneath the right-hand rail. It isn't an isolated patch: a black strip passes from crack to crack, against the light from the windows. Behind it, boards rise one by one.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The doorframe shifts with a bang behind them. The door swings inward, straight at Wendy. She jumps clear of the threshold; Gideon and Pacifica follow, clearing the narrow entrance. It's now several paces away instead of one.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Do you both see...

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The nearest log rolls over its stop. A dull impact travels through their soles. Pacifica steps back sharply and catches her heel on a rail that wasn't behind her a second ago.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Don't go right. The floor is folding there.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: I see it. I was checking another way.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Check this one. Where there are still boards.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He points to a narrow space beside the wall. Pacifica nods; she doesn't feel like arguing. Wendy is already stepping off the nearest rail. The bored look leaves her face.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: To the wall. Don't jump into the middle. There's nothing under that flooring.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: You could've said that before we came in!

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: It was holding up then.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy doesn't add a joke. She picks up a broken board and lays it across the dark gap. Its far end drops immediately, though the near end stays beneath her boot.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: It isn't a hole. The two edges are moving apart.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy lifts the broken board. It's intact, but now lies diagonally, as though someone moved its far end. No draft comes from the gap; they simply can't make out the supports beneath the floor.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Don't lean over it. We don't know how deep it goes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A crack runs the length of the mill. Pacifica looks up: a heavy chain above the aisle stretches almost horizontal, as though the walls are slowly being pulled apart.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Back. There's nothing else we need to check in here.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The entrance remains open. But three logs now lie between it and Gideon instead of one. The nearest rolls slowly across level flooring, peeling a long pale shaving from the boards.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Gideon checks beneath the first log and immediately backs away. It pins a loose bracket to the floor; the iron crumples like thin wire. They couldn't even crawl through now.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Too late for back. Stairs on the left. There's a walkway along the wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica looks from the stairs to Wendy. Wendy is already heading that way, holding her bag against her side. The black strip under the floor changes direction after her.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: One at a time. Step where I step.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Gideon tests the edge of a board and shifts his weight. Pacifica follows with her arms out for balance. Behind them, a metal stop tears loose and strikes a closed window frame.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The stairs are missing their two bottom steps. Wendy climbs over the gap easily, using the side post. Pacifica pulls herself up after her and only then notices how badly her knees are shaking.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Great. Now we get to see all of it from above.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She tries to smile. It comes out crooked. Gideon stops on the landing without touching the loose railing and waits for her to straighten up.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: We can stop for a second.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: One second. I can walk.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She tests the support with her palm and straightens up on her own. Fear still tightens her throat, but her fingers obey again; she can choose her next step.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Better stand where the brackets are, too. Here.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The raised walkway runs along the wall. Each support has a narrow metal platform; wood begins beyond it. Wendy chooses the metal without even looking down.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: You've clearly been here before.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: So? I'm eighteen. I can take a walk without permission.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: I didn't ask about permission. You knew the walkway was intact.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: It was intact. Can't promise anything now. And I didn't sign up to give tours of rotten sheds.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: When was it intact? Last year? Yesterday? That matters right now.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Less than an hour ago. Came in from that side, went up, walked out to the yard. You could still get out then.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She points toward the dark corner beneath the landing, rather than the main entrance. Pacifica remembers the direction. Wendy was in the mill before them and, for some reason, didn't want to say so.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Gideon looks at her left sleeve. Fresh wood dust marks the elbow, as pale as the broken railing ahead. He glances at the break and says nothing yet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Below, logs converge on the spot they just left. One pins another against a rail. Bark splits with a short, wet sound. Pacifica clenches her hands to keep from grabbing the railing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: From above they can see what they missed at the entrance: the black strip curves around stationary crates but crosses the iron rails. It matches no shadow cast by the objects overhead.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Stay close. If the passage changes again, at least we'll be on the same side.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: They aren't moving with the floor. Look: the nails stay put; the log moves across them.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: So this is more than the mill falling apart.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Figure it out outside.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She squeezes past a leaning post. Her bag catches on the edge. Wendy tugs the strap, and the nearest wall support shifts sideways with a metallic groan.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica automatically steps toward the next stretch of flooring. Darkness shows between the boards, broad and even, as though all the daylight beneath them has suddenly been removed.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Pacifica. Stop.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She's still shifting her weight. Gideon catches her forearm. His usual calm expression is gone; he's looking past her at the edge pulling away from the platform.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: BACK! Now!

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica recoils toward the support. The flooring drops without a single crack and hits the logs far below. For another second she keeps her foot raised, unable to believe the empty space ahead.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Okay. You saw it. I understand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Gideon doesn't release her arm straight away. Wendy silently lays a broken railing across the gap as a narrow support. This time nobody hurries to find anything funny.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Three steps to the concrete landing. There's a way down to the gate. Use this to hold on. Don't stand on it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They edge across. On the concrete, Wendy finally frees her caught bag. A short loop slips from a split side pocket, followed by a dull copper edge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy quickly covers the pocket with her hand. Too late: Pacifica is already looking at it. Gideon crouches by the edge of the landing, where he can see the rails below.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: What have you got in there?

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: My belongings. Leave the pocket alone. I'll check what's torn myself.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: When you pulled the strap, the support moved. Before that, the dark strip turned after you.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Everything's moving down there. Pick something else and blame that.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: We haven't blamed anyone yet. But you've been holding that bag tight since this started.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy looks at the torn pocket. Then at the way down: its bottom step already touches a rolling log. She exhales through her teeth and puts the bag on the concrete between her boots.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Keep your hands out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She folds back the fabric herself. Inside is a dark wooden object as long as a palm, broad at the top and tapering downward. A copper rim circles its top, with a short loop attached.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Looks like a plumb bob. Though I don't know if they make wooden ones.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wood is smooth and worn in places. There are no letters or designs. Dirt fills a dent in the copper rim. The object looks ordinary enough to lie among old tools.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Where did you get it?

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: In the woods. Under some washed-out roots, by a ravine. The loop was sticking out, so I pulled it. There wasn't a sign saying not to.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: And you just took it?

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Yes, I took it. About two hours ago. Wanted to look at it in decent light. It looked like an ordinary bit of wood. I wasn't staying in that ravine to study it.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: When did you notice things getting strange? Before you pulled it out, or afterwards?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy looks from him to the exit. A stubborn expression appears, one Pacifica recognizes from her own arguments. Wendy clearly has an uncomfortable answer already; she doesn't want to say it.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Afterwards. The path got longer. I thought I'd taken a wrong turn and cut through the yard. The passage there wasn't where it should be either.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: So that's why you were sitting by the lumber and going nowhere.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: I was checking whether everything would go back. Then you two turned up with questions.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica opens her mouth, but Gideon raises a hand. Metal creaks beneath the landing. He waits for the sound to stop and points to the empty space beside the bag.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Move it a little. Don't lift the object. Just the bag, along the concrete.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: And if everything collapses?

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Stop at the first movement. We've already seen what happens when it's jerked.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy pushes the bag a few inches to the right. Below, the outer rail crawls across the boards in the same direction. Pacifica sees the pale strip it leaves behind and draws a sharp breath.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Stop. That's enough.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy stops the bag. The rail stops. A distant log keeps rolling and crashes into it; keeping the bag still doesn't make the mill safe.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Its weight couldn't move a rail through concrete. And the direction matched. This is connected to what's inside.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Why that thing? You haven't even seen the rest of my junk.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: You found it today. Today distances started disappearing here. We can check the rest when we aren't about to get crushed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy runs a finger along the pocket's edge and falls silent. She still shields the object from their hands, but no longer pretends to find the conversation amusing.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: You knew what was happening here, and still kept quiet while we went inside?

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: I didn't invite you in. You wanted to investigate, so you did. Now I want out too. That'll have to do for now.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: We don't know exactly what it does. But we'd better avoid any sudden movements.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: I understood the first time. The bag stays with me.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Then hold it steady. And stop deciding what you don't need to tell us.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy lifts the bag slowly with both hands and holds it against her stomach. A low scrape travels beneath the concrete. Below, the dark strip reaches the foot of the stairs and stays there, covering the last bottom step.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The stairs lead to a cross aisle in front of the gate. The bright gap beneath it is only a few yards away. Pacifica watches it, making herself see the route rather than the logs on either side.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: The gate slides right. The bottom groove's clogged, so pull the upper handle first.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Another useful thing you somehow only mention at the last second.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: I told you how it opens. Are you going out or arguing with me right here?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy steps off the concrete without letting go of the bag. A distant log turns across the aisle. She stops at once. The log keeps moving, but the gap between it and the gate stops narrowing.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Movement changes the distance. But something that's already rolling won't stop on its own.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Above them, a chain with an empty grapple pulls taut. The grapple swings into a post. Rust spills from its bracket, making that side of the wall unsafe to hold on to.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Stay out from under the grapple. If it breaks loose, it'll fall across the whole aisle.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Heard you. I'm not dropping the bag. Watch everything else.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He speaks quickly, watching both ends of the aisle. The usual drawl is gone from his voice. Pacifica notices and stops wasting breath arguing with Wendy.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Get to the handle first. Then everybody out. Nobody tries to carry anything else away.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She squeezes between the railing and the end of a log, a hand's width from the wood. The board beneath her boot bends, but Pacifica doesn't jump: she slowly transfers her weight to a crossbeam.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Gideon follows the same beam, holding a bolt in the wall. Wendy comes last. When the strap slips off her shoulder, she catches it with her elbow before the bag can swing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Halfway across, Gideon stops: a protruding nail has caught his trouser leg. He crouches, carefully frees the fabric, and gestures for Pacifica to continue. She waits until he's standing. Neither comments on the delay.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy watches over his shoulder, then steps onto the cleared beam. The usual comment about being slow never comes. She only checks whether there's room for another step.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Gate. Now.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica pulls the upper handle with both hands. The gate reluctantly gives. Cold air smelling of damp earth rushes through the gap, and she almost laughs with relief.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then metal strikes outside. The gate slides back toward her fingers. Pacifica snatches her hand away. The impact runs through the mill, shaking dust from above.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: The side rail's twisted. It'll slam shut again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica looks at the landing behind them. A fallen board blocks the lower steps; they can't climb back up. She makes herself turn toward the gate, where there's still light.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Wendy, once we start, don't change direction without warning. Even if you see another way out.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Then talk fast. The beam under my feet is already moving.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them, a stop tears loose with a crack. Two logs begin closing over the aisle. The black strip moves between the boards below, now stretching toward Wendy and the bag.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: One pull won't be enough. We need to hold the gate or find a gap between the logs.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: And the bag can't swing. Everything moves farther each time.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy presses the bag against her side and looks at the narrow exit. This time she waits for someone to finish speaking. A new pale crack opens in the floor before the gate.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Gideon, together. Grab higher. Keep your fingers clear of the edge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They pull the gate with their feet braced against the crossbeam. Gideon shifts his grip, and Pacifica feels the weight finally spread between them.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Holding. Wendy, the bottom stop's jammed under the roller.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy pins the bag under her elbow and kicks the broken piece free. The gate releases, bearing down on the children's arms. They hold it long enough for Wendy to squeeze outside.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: One at a time! Don't shove. There's only one gap.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica lets Gideon through, then slips after him. From outside, he holds the upper handle until the last moment. The gate hits its frame behind her.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica touches her elbow to his shoulder, checking he's beside her. He gives a brief nod and steps away with her, clearing the space before the gate.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Hands okay?

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Yes. Next time we hold something lighter.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: There's a gap behind the nearest log. Follow the pale board, then left to the handle.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: That's a dead end.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: It was. Look at the dust: the far log's moving away. We can get through now.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy looks where he points and gives a brief nod. She goes first, holding the bag carefully. Pacifica watches the nearest log while Gideon judges the timing.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Now. Don't run. Two more steps.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They cross the opening. Wendy leans on the handle; Pacifica jams a board beneath the gate. Gideon goes through last, before the log covers his footprints.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Fine. Good timing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica looks again at the opening he chose. It's already gone. She breathes out and lowers the hand still pointing the way outside.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She says it while already turning away. Gideon doesn't ask her to repeat it. The broken board shoots out behind them, and the gate slams shut.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Shorten the strap. Hold the bag against your back so the object can't swing.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Just stay out of it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica shows her empty hands and takes the loose end of the strap. Wendy tightens the buckle herself. The bag now rests snugly below her shoulder blade, pinned by her forearm.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: The rail's stopped. Move together. No sudden movements.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The logs keep rolling, but the exit stops receding. Gideon pulls a splinter from the bottom groove. Wendy pulls the handle with her free hand while Pacifica braces the gate with her shoulder.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Now. Everyone out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They edge through without breaking stride. Wendy comes out last. She checks the strap and pulls away from Pacifica as soon as she releases the bag's edge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The buckle holds the weight. Wendy starts to turn her shoulder, then stops when she sees the gate move. She takes another slow step before letting herself breathe out.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: That's it. I've got it from here.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: On this side of the gate the ground is firm and still. Pacifica steps away from the wall and stops with her hands on her knees. Only now can she take a full breath.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Gideon stands nearby, listening to the crashing inside. His fingers are still tense, as though he's holding on to something. He straightens them one at a time and checks the outer wall for cracks.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Everybody's out. Good. Then farther from the wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A long crack comes from the mill. Behind a cloudy window, a beam falls slowly. The frame pushes outward and hangs at an impossible angle. They move several more steps away.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Don't bunch up in front of the door. If that gate comes loose, it'll come this way.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica turns toward her, ready with a sharp answer, but only nods. Wendy checks her bag, then looks at the door. She looks angry and intensely focused.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: Now you're going to show us the ravine where you found it.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Now I'm getting away from this dump. I'll decide what to do with the thing on the way.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: After what just happened, you're still...

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Later. Find the road first.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looks across the yard. Pacifica follows his gaze and slowly straightens. Beyond the gate there should be a gravel lane, a partly collapsed stack of lumber, and a gap in the fence leading to the road.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The lumber stack is there. So is the fence. But fir trees stand between them. Their wet lower branches block the way, and roots extend under the gravel as though they've grown here for decades.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica finds the familiar post beside the lane. It should be a few steps from the gate; a strip of moss now lies between them. An old tin can she noticed earlier still sits at its base.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: It's the same yard. But there's a different stretch of forest between its parts.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: No. I walked through here this morning.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: We saw this yard from outside, too. They weren't here.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wendy steps toward the fence. The bag shifts slightly, and the gap between two trunks narrows. She stops before Pacifica can call out to her.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Don't. I can see it.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: We can't go back into the mill. We can't follow the wall either: logs are jammed against the fence there. For now, that gap's all we have.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He doesn't suggest running. Pacifica checks the right side, Wendy the left. There really is no other exit. The road should be beyond the trees, but no strip of asphalt shows between the branches.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The sky over the forest is still bright, but the yard is already in twilight. A long shadow from the nearest fir crosses the toes of her boots. The other shadows point the opposite way.

lines.speaker: Pacifica
lines.text: We got out of the mill. We can get out of here too.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This time her confidence sounds more like a decision than a promise. Pacifica no longer takes the first step without checking where the other two are looking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She speaks steadily, though she stares too hard at the trees. Gideon moves to one side, leaving room for both of them to retreat. Wendy doesn't try to go first again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A scraping comes from beyond the fence. Heavy wood drags across gravel, slowly, with pauses. The sound passes behind one trunk, then another, approaching the narrow gap ahead.

lines.speaker: Gideon
lines.text: Wendy. Keep the bag still.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She holds it with both hands. The hidden object's copper rim touches the buckle with a faint clink. Beyond the trees, the scraping stops at once, as though something has paused to listen.

lines.speaker: Wendy
lines.text: Now what?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pacifica doesn't get to answer. Something heavy lifts off the gravel beyond the fence. Nothing is visible through the branches, but the nearest trunks slowly move apart, opening a path straight toward Wendy.
